CYP2D6.gene_description: Cytochrome P450 2D6 — metabolizes ~25% of clinically used drugs including tricyclics, SSRIs, opioids (codeine, tramadol), beta-blockers, and antipsychotics. Chip-based genotyping misses whole-gene deletion (*5) and duplications (*xN), so phenotype calls from 23andMe should be labeled as tentative.

*4.description: Splice defect; most common no-function allele in Europeans (~21% allele frequency)

*10.description: Decreased function; most common reduced-function allele in East Asians (~40%)

*17.description: Decreased function; most common in African-descent populations

chip_limitations: CYP2D6*5 (whole-gene deletion) requires copy number detection — cannot be called from array data
CYP2D6 duplications (*1xN, *2xN, etc. — ultrarapid-metabolizer-causing) require copy number detection

CYP2C19.gene_description: Cytochrome P450 2C19 — metabolizes clopidogrel, PPIs, SSRIs, tricyclics, and voriconazole. Unlike CYP2D6, star alleles here are cleanly callable from common SNPs.

*2.description: Splice defect, no function; most common no-function allele (~15% Europeans, ~30% East Asians)

*3.description: Stop codon; no function; common in East Asians (~5%)

chip_limitations: Rare star alleles (*4, *5, *6, *8) are not consistently genotyped on 23andMe chips
